newsitem.title: CUBA: U.S. citizen detained in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. citizen detained in Cuba.

text.p: A U.S. citizen was under arrest in Cuba on suspicion of carrying out "acts contrary to the constitutional order," Cuban officials said on Thursday.

Rafael Dausa, deputy head of the Foreign Ministry's North America section, said Walter Van der Veer was being held in the State Security department. Dausa, quoted by the Cuban news agency Prensa Latina, did not say when he was arrested.
Dausa said the U.S. citizen was arrested because there were indications of some illegal activity but he gave no details of what this was.

Cuban official sources said it appeared Van der Veer was being investigated for a possible offence against state security. This could mean something like links with dissident groups or bringing in material viewed as subversive with a view to distributing it.
Dausa denied U.S. news reports that Van der Veer was in Cuba on a humanitarian or charity mission.

But in Miami, Tony Bryant, leader of exile group Commandos L, said Van der Veer went to Cuba on a "humanitarian" mission about four months ago. Bryant said the U.S. mission in Cuba told the group Van der Veer was arrested about a month ago for alleged crimes against the state.
"My concern is that he will be tried for crimes against the government of Fidel Castro," Bryant said. "My concern is that he might be executed."
Bryant, a former Black Panther militant, said he asked the U.S. government to intervene to win Van der Veer's freedom.
Commandos L is one of several Miami-based paramilitary groups dedicated to Castro's overthrow. Formed in the early 1960s, it mounted occasional armed attacks in Cuban territory.

Dausa said U.S. authorities were informed of the situation and permission had been given for consular access to Van der Veer. Officials at the U.S. Interests Section in Havana were not immediately available for comment.

Few U.S. citizens visit Cuba because it is subject to a longstanding U.S. economic embargo. U.S. visitors are mostly from charities or academic institutions on licensed visits or tourists ignoring the embargo.
